body:
Private equity firm Endless has acquired residential developer Weston Homes.

Established in 1987, Weston Homes operates across London and the home counties. Following the acquisition, the housebuilder will retain its own brand and senior management team.

This includes chief executive Peter Gore, group finance director Stuart Thomas and group development director Steve Hatton. Funding provided by Endless will be used support the group’s existing developments and future pipeline.

Weston Homes’ founder and former chief executive Bob Weston will step back as chairman as part of the move, but will continue to play an active role in the group going forward.

In the developer’s latest financial results, in the year to 31 July 2025, Weston Homes reported a pre-tax loss of £4.5m, up on £14.5m the prior year.

Notable schemes under Weston Homes’ belt include a £110.1m build-to-rent (BTR) scheme in Bracknell Beeches, Berkshire, and an 85-home BTR development at Town Quay in Barking.

Gore, who was appointed to the role in 2024, said: “This marks an exciting new growth chapter for Weston Homes. With Endless’s backing, we have the investment and support to build on the strengths of the group, deliver our existing developments and invest in new opportunities for the future.

“We have a strong brand, an experienced team and a clear ambition to grow the business sustainably over the coming years, while continuing to deliver the quality and standards our customers associate with Weston Homes.”

Other key schemes on the company’s schedule include Thornwood Park, just outside Epping in Essex. The project has a gross development value of £33.5m and will offer a collection of 62 two- to five-bedroom family homes in a 10-acre countryside setting.
